clue.text: Lay out in one's underwear

parts.note: taken as written
a vest is an undershirt in British usage

explanation.surface: Someone is being caught out while dressed only in their underclothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay out money is to spend it in the hope of a return.

clue.text: Swell location for someone on strike

explanation.surface: A pleasant spot for a striking worker to stand, perhaps by the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batsman on strike stands IN the CREASE, the marked line at the wicket; read as one word it means a swelling or growth.
explanation.definitionFit: To swell is to grow larger; in cricket the striking batsman stands within the crease.

clue.text: Leave the profession hardly changed

indicators.note: only a single letter is altered, so the word is barely different

parts.note: a vocation is a calling or profession

explanation.surface: Someone quits their career with little difference to show for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hardly changed' swaps just one letter: the O of VOCATION becomes A.
explanation.definitionFit: Leave is time off work, a holiday.

clue.text: Raise animals for the stage

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word means reading it upwards, so backwards

parts.note: pets are domestic animals

explanation.surface: A farmer breeds livestock to appear in the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage is a step in a process.

clue.text: Get rid of wicked, wicked woman

parts.note: to shed is to cast off
evil means wicked

explanation.surface: An instruction to cast out wickedness, and then a description of a bad woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A malicious, spiteful woman is called a fiend in female form.

clue.text: Coins as distinct from notes?

parts.note: metal coins are solid money, unlike flimsy paper banknotes; the phrase also means a strong, stable currency

explanation.surface: A question about the difference between metal money and paper money.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase normally means a stable, trusted currency; here it is read literally as solid money.

clue.text: Drugs advice for the unfit

explanation.surface: Guidance on narcotics given to people who are out of shape.
explanation.walkthrough: Dope is both narcotics and inside information, such as racing tips on which horse is not fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcotics are slang dope; dope is also slang for information or tips.

clue.text: Initially, it comes between players at Wimbledon, say

definitions.text: Initially, it comes between players at Wimbledon, say

parts.words: Initially, it comes between players at Wimbledon, say
parts.note: in its abbreviated form, a single letter v, the word sits between two names in a tennis match listing

explanation.surface: Something separates the competitors at a tennis championship.
explanation.definitionFit: A match is listed as one player against the other, with the Latin word for against abbreviated to v.

clue.text: Amateur — could be any male lacking energy

indicators.note: the letters might be rearranged into a new word, so this signals an anagram

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark that any man could do an amateur's job without much energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes E from the letters of ANY MALE; the remaining ANYMAL is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A layperson is a non-professional, someone without expert training.

clue.text: Tom retains a revolutionary's prestige

indicators.note: the outer word keeps the other inside it

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: Someone named Tom holds on to a rebel's status.
explanation.definitionFit: Cachet is the distinction or status that brings respect.

clue.text: Quality goods

explanation.surface: A two-word description of fine merchandise.
explanation.definitionFit: A property is an attribute; property also means possessions.

clue.text: Kind of order revealed in NOP

parts.note: the letters N, O and P stand in the sequence they take in the ABC

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what system three capital letters follow.
explanation.walkthrough: N, O, P are consecutive letters, showing the order used in dictionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Order by letters of the ABC is one kind of sorting.

clue.text: Little Elizabeth loses her head to an artist

indicators.note: the first letter of the name is cut off

parts.note: Betty is a pet form of the name Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A girl called Elizabeth is beheaded for the sake of a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: William Etty was an English painter of the 19th century.
explanation.definitionFit: Etty was a painter, known for his nudes.

clue.text: The Vatican for instance doesn't need a station

indicators.note: a letter is left out of the word

parts.note: the Vatican is a papal palace

explanation.surface: The Pope's residence apparently has no need of a railway terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: Station means one's position or rank, as does a place.

clue.text: Tropical island gear for diving, mostly

indicators.note: not all of the word is used, one letter is dropped

parts.note: scuba is underwater breathing apparatus

explanation.surface: Equipment for underwater swimming around a warm island.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuba is a Caribbean island nation.

clue.text: Edge around a garment

explanation.surface: A border running round an item of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To go round the edge of something is to skirt it; a skirt is also clothing worn from the waist.

clue.text: Eastern films often are!

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for East or Eastern
pics is informal for films, pictures

explanation.surface: Movies from the Orient tend to be long sweeping sagas.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand large-scale films, such as many Asian historical dramas, are called by this name.

clue.text: Cure for hiccups?

parts.note: a sudden fright is the folk remedy for hiccups, read as a psychiatric treatment

explanation.surface: A question about a remedy for a spasm of the diaphragm.
explanation.definitionFit: Electroconvulsive treatment has this name; a fright is the traditional way to stop hiccups.

clue.text: Kipling's extremes shown in full measure

parts.note: the first and last letters of the writer's name are K and G, the abbreviation for a metric unit, spelt out at length

explanation.surface: The edges of a writer's name displayed completely.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of mass is a measure.

clue.text: Revised seedings cause some anxiety

indicators.note: the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Changes to tournament seeding cause players to worry.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on edge is nervousness, a measure of anxiety.

clue.text: A difficult issue, so to speak

definitions.text: A difficult issue, so to speak

parts.words: A difficult issue, so to speak
parts.note: issue here means offspring, so a hard-to-handle son or daughter

explanation.surface: An awkward topic or matter under discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue means children, so a troublesome one is a hard-to-manage youngster.

clue.text: Watch your heart!

explanation.surface: A warning to take care of your health.
explanation.definitionFit: Ticker is slang both for a timepiece and for the heart.

clue.text: Insects seen on board, and possibly doorsteps!

indicators.note: being on board a ship puts one inside it

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, the vessel boarded
lice are parasitic insects

explanation.surface: Bugs found aboard a vessel and perhaps on the front steps.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a doorstep is a very thick slice of bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Doorsteps are thick cut portions of bread, examples of the answer.

clue.text: Lied about being unemployed

indicators.note: the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone fibbed regarding being out of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle can mean not working, without a job.

clue.text: Old school punishment also applied to staff!

explanation.surface: The cane used on pupils was also used on the teachers.
explanation.walkthrough: A stick is both the cane once used on schoolchildren and a walking staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Caning was traditional school discipline; a staff is a walking pole.

clue.text: Places return in nostalgic old age

indicators.note: the concealed letters are read backwards
the letters are found inside the words

explanation.surface: Elderly people go back to familiar locations out of nostalgia.
explanation.definitionFit: Loci is the Latin plural for locations.

clue.text: Meet in a bar

parts.note: bar can mean except, as does but

explanation.surface: Arranging to rendezvous at a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: To abut is to adjoin, to touch at a border.

clue.text: Cause trouble and it might mean gaol

explanation.surface: Making mischief could land someone in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir is to agitate; stir is also slang for prison.

clue.text: Pass to goalkeeper, maybe as a bribe

explanation.surface: A footballer plays the ball back to the keeper as a corrupt payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Kicking the ball backwards is a pass; an illicit payment is also known by this name.

clue.text: Die like famous person on the Victory

parts.note: a star is a celebrity
VE stands for Victory in Europe

explanation.surface: Someone dies like a celebrity aboard Nelson's flagship.
explanation.walkthrough: HMS Victory is Nelson's ship, but here Victory just gives VE, as in VE Day.
explanation.definitionFit: To starve is to die from lack of food.

clue.text: Make new home in foreign street, with the French

indicators.note: something foreign is strange, so the letters are made unfamiliar

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: Moving abroad to a street in France.
explanation.definitionFit: To resettle is to move to a different place to live.

clue.text: Unsmiling American could be warmed by it

parts.note: prim means stiffly formal and unsmiling
US is the United States

explanation.surface: A stern American could be thawed out by something.
explanation.walkthrough: A Primus is a portable camping stove.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand of camping stove gives heat to someone cold.
